_comment: trustfoundry-case-name-lookup scorer config.
cutoffs=[1,3,5,10]. The scorer's validateConfig throws at startup on any other
value -- SUPPORTED_CUTOFFS is pinned to this set in the scorer adapter, so this
is deliberate and not a knob this config can turn.
headline_cutoff=1. The headline question for a case-name lookup is 'did the top
result carry the wanted case's name?'. hit@3, hit@5, and hit@10 are reported
beside it, from the same `cutoffs` list, so the drop-off past the top slot is
visible -- that shape is exactly where a weaker backend reveals itself: a
provider that only catches up by rank 3 or 5 is doing real work the headline
alone would hide.
Negative rows are excluded from the headline by construction: buildSummary
aggregates only kind=positive into `overall`, and reports negatives separately
as negatives_overall, so a false-positive rate cannot dilute a recall-shaped
number.
Every scored row also reports a caption-deduplicated `dedupedHitRank` and
`distinctInTop5` alongside the raw `hitRank`, and every aggregate (`overall`,
each `by_tier.<tier>`, each `by_axis.<axis>`) reports a parallel `deduped_hit_at`
beside `hit_at` -- a page-quality view of the same ranking. Dedup never changes
whether a row counts as a hit, only how deep a user had to look past repeated
captions to reach a new one.
api_request_limit is forwarded by the runner into providerConfig.limit when the
provider config does not set one. TrustFoundry's public API caps limit at 25.
WHERE TO READ EACH NUMBER. A published bundle's per-row `score.hit_at` is an
object keyed `hit@K` for exactly this scorer's configured cutoffs, so hit@1,
hit@3, hit@5, and hit@10 are all present there by name. The same set is
aggregated in `summary.overall.hit_at['hit@K']` of scores.json, report.json,
and a published bundle's result.json -- that summary is built by this scorer
from its configured cutoffs, and it is what `benchmark verify-result`
recomputes and checks.
Per-row, hit@K for any K is also recoverable from `score.hit_rank` (hit@K is
hit_rank != null and hit_rank <= K).
